comments.note: workflow-helpers.ts: checkRevalidationGuard() takes WorkPackageDetail as its first parameter (accessing only wp.pipelines internally), consistent with the WP spec. However, all other pipeline-state guards in this file (hasDownstreamFail, hasNewUpstreamPassSince, hasDownstreamReengagedSince) take Pipeline[] directly. A future refactor could standardize the signature to Pipeline[] for consistency, or conversely migrate existing helpers to WorkPackageDetail for richer context access. Either direction is fine — just worth noting the mixed convention.

workflow-helpers.ts: The getUpstreamTypes import was added to the existing import statement from pipeline-maps.js. The file now imports both getDownstreamTypes and getUpstreamTypes from the same module — clean and consistent with the project pattern.

summary: Reviewed checkRevalidationGuard() in workflow-helpers.ts against §11.1 spec algorithm — faithful line-by-line mapping confirmed.

Algorithm correctness: all 9 spec steps implemented correctly. Temporal boundary (>=) uses inclusive semantics matching spec intent. auto_cancelled exclusion applied on both baseline and prereq paths.
Signature: WorkPackageDetail input is spec-compliant. The mixed-signature convention with sibling Pipeline[]-based helpers is a known, documented non-blocking pattern.
Integration: function is correctly scoped to this WP as a pure export only; no call sites expected until WP-008.
No blocking issues found. Three low-priority non-blocking observations carried forward from Developer + QA — see comments.

comments.note: workflow-helpers.ts: checkRevalidationGuard() takes WorkPackageDetail while all sibling guards (hasDownstreamFail, hasNewUpstreamPassSince, hasDownstreamReengagedSince) take Pipeline[] directly. The spec prescribes this signature, so the current form is correct. Worth standardising in a future refactor — either migrate all helpers to WorkPackageDetail for richer context access, or strip wp.pipelines at the call-site and pass Pipeline[] here.

workflow-helpers.test.ts: Test 'returns null for normal progression (prereq PASS post-dates any prior run)' (line ~479) exercises the first-run path a second time — no prior qa pipeline exists, so the guard exits at Step 1 rather than via the timestamp comparison path. The test passes correctly but its name implies it is verifying Step 3 (fresh prereq bypass). A future rename to 'returns null on first run — no prior qa pipeline (duplicate)' or replacing it with a genuine fresh-prereq scenario would improve test literacy.

workflow-helpers.test.ts: The equal-timestamp boundary case (prereqCompletedAt === baselineStartedAt → null) is confirmed correct by QA manual inspection but has no dedicated test. The >= comparison in Step 3 makes this explicit in code, but adding a test asserting that equal timestamps are treated as 'fresh' would document this non-obvious invariant for future maintainers.

workflow-helpers.ts: checkRevalidationGuard() does not guard against pipelineType === prerequisite (same-stage call). This is a logical invariant violation — no stage can be its own prerequisite — and cannot occur at current call-sites. No action needed now, but documenting the invariant in the JSDoc as a @throws or @param note would make future integration safer.
